tasks.title: Vector
tasks.statement: Define a class Vector(x, y) with the operators + (addition), - (subtraction), * by a number (scaling), == (equality by value) and a method __repr__ that returns «Vector(1, 2)». The operators return NEW vectors.
tasks.hint: __add__, __sub__, __mul__, __eq__, __repr__: each one returns a result and does not change self.

tasks.title: Money
tasks.statement: Define a class Money(amount): objects are equal if their amounts are equal (__eq__); they can be sorted (__lt__); they can be used as dictionary keys (__hash__).

tasks.title: Playlist
tasks.statement: Define a class Playlist(songs): len(p) returns the number of songs, p[i] returns the song by number, and "title in p" checks whether a song is present. An empty playlist must count as false in a condition.
tasks.hint: __len__, __getitem__ and __contains__; bool() relies on __len__ by itself.

tasks.title: Temperature
tasks.statement: Define a class Temperature(celsius): a property celsius with validation (below -273.15 is a ValueError, including when the object is created) and a computed read-only property fahrenheit: celsius * 9 / 5 + 32.
tasks.hint: In __init__ assign self.celsius = celsius so that the setter runs; store the value in self._celsius.

tasks.title: A person from a string
tasks.statement: Define a class Person(name, age) and a class method from_string(s) that parses a string like «Аня,20» and returns a Person (the age is a number). The method __str__ returns «Аня (20)».
tasks.hint: @classmethod def from_string(cls, s): name, age = s.split(','); return cls(name, int(age)).

tasks.title: Circle
tasks.statement: Define a class Circle(radius): a property radius (greater than 0, otherwise ValueError) and a read-only property area equal to 3.14159 * radius ** 2.
tasks.hint: A property without a setter can't be assigned to: Python raises AttributeError by itself.

tasks.title: Versions
tasks.statement: Define a class Version(text): text is a string like «1.2.10». Versions are compared by numbers, not by text: 1.2.10 is greater than 1.2.9. You need __lt__, __eq__ and __str__ (which returns the original string).
tasks.hint: Compare tuples of numbers: tuple(int(p) for p in self.text.split('.')); for > Python reverses __lt__ by itself.
